title: Defer all universal rarity proportions
scope: Project governance for any future work that proposes rarity proportions; no present setting or object family is quantified and no distribution is silently inherited by an independent work.
approval_evidence: The Author instructed that rarity distribution be recorded as an Author-approved DEFERRED decision with the stated activation prerequisites on 2026-08-12.
question: Should the project assign universal rarity proportions before a concrete object family, rarity dimension, denominator, population, period, and evidence are defined?
selection: Defer rarity distribution. Define no universal proportions. Activate a scoped rarity-distribution decision only after defining the object type, rarity dimension, eligible denominator, population, period, and evidence base.
alternatives: Assign one universal rarity ladder and proportions now; rejected as undefined and over-broad.
Defer all proportions until the six activation prerequisites are defined; selected.
rationale: Rarity is multidimensional and denominator-sensitive. A universal percentage would conflate unlike objects, recognition rules, populations, periods, and evidence bases before any real setting exists.
evidence: litrpg-system/cal0/canonical/litrpg-system-specification.md: rarity is typed and scope-dependent rather than a universal power tier.
litrpg-system/cal0/guide/litrpg-system-residual-uncertainty-register.md: rarity proportions remain a world-level input.
consequences: No universal rarity proportions may be inserted into setting, character, story, or population models.
Rarity distributions must be separately scoped for a defined object type and rarity dimension.
No distribution work begins until the eligible denominator, population, period, and evidence base are explicit.
This deferral creates no setting fact and supplies no default percentages.
residual_unknowns: Population and observation period are undefined.
reopening_conditions: A proposal defines the object type, rarity dimension, eligible denominator, population, period, and evidence base.
The Author explicitly activates a scoped rarity-distribution decision after those prerequisites are met.
